Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 27
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: Middle Eastern
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Physical Therapist
  trauma_type: Sexual assault
  pcl5: 49

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Olfactory (Cologne/Perfume): A specific perfume or cologne, Somatic (Pain): Physical pain in a part of the body, Sexual Situations: Sexual situations or intimacy
  Maladaptive Strategies: Dissociation: I pretend it happened to someone else, Avoid Thinking: Thinking about the event, Body Monitoring: constantly check body for signs of danger or injury
  Threat: Startle Response: Feeling jumpy or easily startled, Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly, Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
  Negative Appraisals: Lost Emotions: I will never be able to feel normal emotions again, Can't Rely on Self: I can't rely on myself, Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body

Vignette:
Amir's eyes would often glaze over when he recounted the night that changed everything. It was a typical Friday evening, and he had met up with friends at a local bar after work. He remembered feeling carefree, laughing and joking with his friends as they sipped their drinks. But as the night wore on, Amir's memory became hazy. He vaguely recalled stumbling out of the bar, disoriented and confused, only to find himself in an unfamiliar room, surrounded by strangers. The next thing he knew, he was waking up in a hospital bed, his body throbbing with pain. As Amir slowly pieced together the events of that night, he began to realize the extent of what had happened. He had been sexually assaulted, and the experience left him reeling. Simple things like walking down the street or interacting with strangers became daunting tasks. The smell of a specific perfume or cologne would transport him back to that fateful night, leaving him feeling disoriented and vulnerable. Amir tried to push the memories away, pretending it had happened to someone else. He'd dissociate from his body, watching himself go through the motions of daily life as if he were an outside observer. But the physical pain persisted, a constant reminder of what he'd endured. Amir would often find himself wincing in anticipation of pain, even when there was none. His body had become a source of anxiety, a fragile vessel that might betray him at any moment. As a physical therapist, Amir's work required him to be attuned to his patients' bodies, but now he struggled to connect with them on a physical level. He'd flinch when they touched him unexpectedly or react with alarm when someone moved suddenly nearby. His startle response had become so pronounced that his wife would often joke about it, trying to catch him off guard just to see how he'd react. But beneath the surface, Amir was grappling with darker fears. He felt ashamed of what had happened to his body, as if it were somehow tainted or damaged beyond repair. He couldn't shake the feeling that he'd never be able to experience normal emotions again, that he was forever trapped in a state of numbness. The thought sent him spiraling into despair, making him question whether he could ever trust himself or his own instincts. Amir's relationship with his wife began to suffer as well. Intimacy became a source of anxiety, rather than comfort. He'd find himself withdrawing from her touch, fearing that it would trigger another flashback or episode of dissociation. His wife tried to be understanding, but Amir could sense the frustration building between them. It was only when Amir's symptoms began to affect his work that he realized he needed help. Patients were starting to notice his distraction and edginess, and his performance was suffering as a result. One particularly difficult session with a patient had left him shaken, forcing him to confront the toll his PTSD was taking on his life. As Amir sat in his therapist's office for the first time, he felt a mix of emotions: fear, shame, but also a glimmer of hope. He knew it wouldn't be easy, but he was willing to face the darkness head-on, to learn how to reclaim his body and his sense of self. The thought sent a shiver down his spine, but for the first time in months, Amir felt like he might finally be able to breathe again.
